 Mavs Notes: Irving, Powell, Cisse, Injuries, Johnson
 By Luke Adams |
 at October 20, 2026 3:29 pm 
 LeBron James will turn 42 years old two months into the 2026/27 season, but Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving can’t envision himself emulating his former teammate and still being in the NBA by the time he reaches that age, he said on Monday, per Christian Clark of The Athletic .
 Irving, who is entering his 16th season and will turn 35 in March, said he still loves playing basketball but feels as if the NBA has become “less human” and “more robotic” since he first entered the league, adding that he doesn’t feel the same way about the “hoopla that goes into (it)” as he once did.
 “Basketball is an eternal flame,” Irving said. “In terms of the NBA schedule and things of that nature, you have to really be in love with that, too. The weight lifting. The unseen hours. The media prep. Just going in and being ready to play at a high level. Also, you have social media and gambling right now, which is running rampant. It’s not the same NBA I fell in love with as a kid. 
 “… I don’t see myself playing in the NBA at 42, 43. Shout-out to the head honcho (James) over there still going. Even Steph (Curry) . Klay (Thompson) and James (Harden) and KD ( Kevin Durant ). I looked at those guys as big brothers for a while, but now that I’m in this age of 34, 35, I love my manhood and growing as a man more than growing as a basketball player.” 
 Irving holds a $42.4MM player option for the 2027/28 season. If he picks up that option, he’d be 36 years old by the time his current contract expires.
 We have more on the Mavericks:
 In the wake of the team’s decision to waive veteran big man Dwight Powell on Monday, Irving said the longtime Maverick will be “severely missed” and that he “represented a lot here in the city of Dallas,” while head coach Dusty May suggested he wouldn’t be shocked to see Powell land with another NBA team, according to Grant Afseth of Dallas Hoops Journal . “Look, I’m relatively new to the NBA game, so I don’t know the ins and outs and the calendar with moves and things like that,” May said. “So would I be surprised to see Dwight playing somewhere? I wouldn’t. He still has some miles in the tank.” 
 With Dereck Lively II still recovering from foot surgery and Powell no longer in the picture, reserve big man Moussa Cisse should have an opportunity to get some “game minutes” to open the season, May said on Monday. Afseth has the details in another Dallas Hoops Journal story .
 May provided a series of injury updates ahead of Wednesday’s regular season opener vs. Houston on Wednesday, as Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News relays ( via Twitter ). Max Christie (sore foot) practiced on Tuesday and will be available to play on Wednesday, but Tarik Biberovic (right heel bursitis) didn’t practice and will be out. As for big man Santi Aldama , who is coming off foot surgery, he was a partial participant on Tuesday, and while he may not be ready to play on Wednesday, he’s “getting very close,” May said.
 In a series of stories, Curtis , Afseth , and Eddie Sefko of Mavs.com explore how May intends to use lottery pick Morez Johnson Jr. this season and consider what sort of impact the former Michigan standout could have as a rookie. May indicated he expects to use Johnson at both power forward and center. “Right now, injuries at certain positions might dictate where he plays,” the Mavs’ coach said. “But he’s going to be able to play both and eventually just be an interchangeable piece as he expands his offensive game, because defensively he can guard one through five.”
